fields.description:
# The parity flip/agreement criteria are gold-blind, so a candidate is failed for being MORE accurate

## Context / Problem

Criterion (b) of the parity bar has two parts, and BOTH compare the two arms to each other
without ever consulting the gold label that the same corpus carries:

* `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` — `agreement = _rate(pairs, lambda p: p[0].decision == p[1].decision)`
* `src/rebar/llm/parity.py` — `decision_flips = ... a.decision != b.decision` (gold pairs are
  selected on `a.label`, but the label is never used in the COMPARISON)

Recall and false-accept in the same function DO consult `label`. So the bar already knows which
arm is right on every gold item, and criterion (b) deliberately throws that away.

Consequence, measured on the recorded live Bedrock run
(`src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json`, re-scored offline with zero model
calls after the 62ac false-accept fix): all THREE decision flips across both slots are cases
where the CANDIDATE (Bedrock) matches gold and the BASELINE (direct Anthropic) does not.

| slot | case | spec | gold | v1 Anthropic | v2 Bedrock |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| standard | R-drop-column-no-backfill | code-review-db-migrations | block | advisory | **block** |
| frontier | FP-rename-all-callsites-updated | code-review-api-compat | advisory | block | **advisory** |
| frontier | FP-create-index-concurrently | code-review-db-migrations | advisory | block | **advisory** |

Bedrock is correct in 3 of 3. The bar reports these as "decision-level flip(s) on the gold set
(must be 0)" — the criterion documented as never acceptable because "it changes what ships".

The same three disagreements also drive the only other remaining failure: frontier verdict
agreement 0.929. At the scored corpus size of n=28, the 0.95 floor tolerates at most ONE
disagreement anywhere in the corpus (27/28 = 0.964 passes, 26/28 = 0.929 fails), so the
agreement failure is not independent evidence — it is the same two cases counted again.

## Why it matters

This is a gating criterion on rebar's non-inferiority bar. As written it can fail a strictly
better candidate. It is the sibling of bug 62ac (the inverted false-accept metric): both come
from a metric that measures the wrong direction of the same underlying quantity. 62ac is fixed;
this one is not, and it is now the sole remaining blocker on the Bedrock parity slots.

Note this ticket does NOT propose relaxing the bar to let Bedrock pass. It proposes that the
criterion measure what it claims to measure — a regression in what ships — which requires
consulting gold on a gold-labelled corpus.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Decide and document whether criterion (b) should distinguish a gold-IMPROVING flip from a
      gold-REGRESSING one on gold-labelled items, and whether the agreement floor should be
      computed over non-gold items only (where no ground truth exists) or left as is.
- [x] If a change is made, a test pins the direction: a candidate that flips a gold item TOWARD
      the gold label is scored differently from one that flips it AWAY.
- [x] The recorded provider-parity results are re-scored offline against whatever bar results,
      with zero model calls, and the per-slot verdict recorded.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
